articles.summary: AT&T processes 45 billion tokens daily and is actively shifting 60 to 70 percent of that volume to internally hosted open-source models, because at frontier prices the bill for routine summarization and retrieval tasks becomes hundreds of millions of dollars for work that simply does not require frontier capability. The emerging enterprise AI strategy is not about picking the best model but building the routing logic that sends each task to the right model at the right cost.
articles.title: The Enterprise AI Ownership Threshold

articles.summary: July's release is a more focused one, with updates that make day-to-day work more practical across search, project management, and automation. From richer search options in Span Labeling to more flexible export and document management workflows, these improvements are designed to help teams move faster with less friction in both Data Studio and LLM Labs.
articles.title: July 2026 Feature Updates: Smarter Search, Smoother Project Management, and Better Workflow Automation

articles.summary: Gemma crossing 1 billion downloads is a meaningful signal that the open-weight ecosystem is not a niche preference but a mainstream infrastructure choice developers and organizations are actively building around. Capability is no longer defined by model size, and accessibility is proving to be a competitive advantage in its own right.
articles.title: From Open Weights to Browser Use: Celebrating Gemma’s 1B Download Milestone

articles.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI swapping market share positions in a matter of weeks reveals something more important than who is winning: businesses are treating AI providers like a rental market, switching whenever a better model ships. The real competition is not for users but for the integrations, workflows, and switching costs that make customers stay when the next release arrives.
articles.title: The AI Model Market Is Becoming a Rental Market
